turns.content: A close friend owes me a fair amount of money from months ago and keeps not bringing it up, and neither do I. It's starting to poison how I feel every time we hang out.
You want your money back. You already know this. It's clear that not bringing it up is not working. You do need to talk to your friend about the debt.
She just posted about a weekend trip she took, and something in me went cold.
You feel angry. That's true. You want your money back before she spends more on trips. You do need to ask her for it now.
I hate that I seem to care about the money more than the friendship, or at least that's how it feels when I imagine asking.
You want the friendship to be clear of debt. You already know this is about more than money. You do need to say what you want: your money back or a plan to pay it.
We're getting drinks Thursday. I keep telling myself I'll bring it up naturally, knowing full well I won't unless I decide to.
You will bring it up Thursday. You do need to decide to say it: "I want my money back, can we make a plan?"
